canonical_statement: A probability distribution on the real line is infinitely divisible if and only if its characteristic function has a Levy-Khinchin representation, with the representation convention and uniqueness conditions to be fixed by the statement phase.
domain_and_universes: Intended domain: Borel probability measures on R and their complex-valued characteristic functions; exact Lean universes and measure API are not yet selected.
quantifiers: mu: a Borel probability measure on R
equivalently quantified Levy-Khinchin data after its convention is frozen
hypotheses: infinite divisibility means: for every positive natural n, mu is the n-fold convolution power of some probability measure
conclusion: Infinite divisibility is equivalent to existence of valid Levy-Khinchin characteristic-exponent data representing the characteristic function of mu.

alternate_encodings.relationship: classically equivalent candidate under continuity hypotheses

excluded_degenerate_cases: No probability measure is excluded at intake: Dirac laws and zero Gaussian or Levy-measure components remain in scope. The n = 0 convolution convention is not part of infinite divisibility; the exact quantifier is n >= 1.
